target_customer: Gmail users, especially sales, recruiting and networking professionals
problem: Email gave no context about who you were writing to. Rapportive showed profile photos, location, job and social links inside Gmail.
business_model: free Gmail plugin with a path to paid CRM features; exited before monetizing

founders.name: Rahul Vohra
previous_startups: an earlier startup in a Cambridge UK co-working space, name not stated
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CEO; he later founded Superhuman.

founders.name: Martin Kleppmann
founders.background_notes: From his own 2011 interview: from Germany, met the other founders at a Cambridge co-working space.

founders.name: Sam Stokes
previous_startups: an earlier startup with Rahul Vohra, name not stated
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no background.

exit.reason: Price reported as around 15 million dollars in cash by sources cited by TechCrunch; the company did not confirm it. Deal confirmed by Rapportive on 22 February 2012.

competitors.name: Xobni
competitors.what: Outlook add-in that surfaces contact information, compared to Rapportive as Xobni for Gmail

competitors.name: Gist
competitors.what: Google Apps contextual gadget showing profiles of Gmail contacts

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser extension injecting into Gmail's changing interface plus aggregating social data across services at scale, which took careful engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Depended on Gmail and on public social profile data. Gist and others offered similar gadgets, and LinkedIn could replicate the data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: LinkedIn acquired it in February 2012, did little new development, removed Raplets, notes and the Google Apps gadget in July 2014, and later folded it into Sales Navigator for Gmail.

market_need_then: Gmail had a huge user base and no contact context; TheNextWeb called Rapportive a slick social CRM tool in March 2010, and Google opened contextual gadgets in May 2010.

identity.voice_and_tone: Relationship focused; the YC copy talks about establishing rapport with contacts.

branding.brand_signature: Raplets (third party extensions to the Rapportive sidebar)

rebrands.why: LinkedIn later folded the product into Sales Navigator; the year comes from a search summary and is unverified

branding.community_and_virality: Widely covered by TechCrunch, TheNextWeb and Xconomy in 2010, and Raplets gave a small developer ecosystem. No merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known among Gmail power users and in tech press, and the name evoked its function, but it was an add-on to someone else's product and not a household brand.

outcome_analysis: Rapportive spread as a free Gmail plugin right as Google opened contextual gadgets in May 2010, raised a 1 million dollar seed from CRV and many angels, and sold to LinkedIn in February 2012 for about 15 million dollars in cash. It was a modest exit with a product that LinkedIn left largely undeveloped before cutting features in 2014 and sunsetting it. The founders used the sale to later build Superhuman.
notes: Seed of 1M and investors from TechCrunch Feb 2012; aggregators date the round Aug 2010 but no opened source does, so date is the year only. Price of around 15M is reported by sources and not confirmed by the companies. The final sunset year (March 2016) is unverified; search summaries gave the date without a year. Founder prior employers and education for Vohra and Stokes were not found. Rapportive's own homepage is no longer a standalone product, and it was not separately fetched; site status is taken from sunset coverage.
